personal.background:
Alex Kauffman is a designer focused on clarity, interaction, and systems-thinking. With a BFA in New Media Design from RIT, he blends creative direction and product thinking to design tools that support thoughtful, long-term growth.

He’s currently exploring roles in product design and visual systems — aiming to contribute to meaningful products, not just fast-moving ideas. His dream role is helping Microsoft’s Accessibility team improve the Xbox gaming experience for diverse players — or working with platforms like Toast to make everyday payments more accessible for all.

Outside of design, Alex is getting into motocross (MX) as a new hobby. He also enjoys traveling to different countries, meeting new people, and trying unfamiliar things — always chasing experiences that expand perspective.

personal.dream job:
My dream is to work on accessibility at Microsoft’s Xbox team or Apple’s Human Interface Accessibility group—creating technology that levels the playing field and helps people move through life with fewer barriers.

My motto: Accessibility is about building the right tools for users, while inclusion is about supporting their emotional experience. Both are essential to truly empower people through technology.
personal.goal: My 5-year goal is to grow in a full-time product design and engineering role while contributing visionary ideas and production support to teams building accessible, mission-driven products at companies like Apple, Disney Research, or Toast.

personal.weakness:
Ohhh, a trick hot question... I naturally gravitate toward concepting and systems thinking more than pixel-perfect polish. I'm strongest when I'm exploring ideas, shaping flows, and figuring out the experience logic.

Because I know that about myself, I'm intentional about collaborating with designers who thrive in high-fidelity craftsmanship. It creates a good balance: I move fast on direction and structure, and I partner with detail-oriented teammates to elevate the final visual finish.
personal.deadlines:
When I work with tight deadlines, I make sure I really understand my project scope and what the needs are. I tend to deliver my concepts in 3 different levels to help step down what is MVP thinking vs what is a sky-high approach.

This helps me boil out things we can focus on later when we have tight deadlines.

personal.successful project:
My most successful project is Duolingo ASL. I showcased to Duolingo a concept that helps open a new streamline of revenue by targeting non-verbal language learning. The amount of statistics and research shows that people need basic accessibility to learn sign language — it proves we need that to happen. Duolingo is a platform that helps understand how users learn in non-verbal language to benefit other purposes of industry use.

I learned this project showcased that accessibility + purpose = results. My LinkedIn has gained over 8k likes and many comments. It proves my strong vision aligns with what users need — that's what makes a successful project. I didn't have all the flows or perfect pixel layouts. I had a strong foundation of what users needed that made good results to build with.

Vigor Fitness.title: Vigor Fitness
Vigor Fitness.description: Reimagning fitness in a gamification way to avoid burnouts.

content.wideTitle: The challenge was to create a mobile fitness platform designed for phone screens with our own liberty.

content.intro_paragraph:
Vigor helps busy Americans stay active by turning everyday movement into real progress. Through user research, I shaped a gamified system that transforms daily energy into meaningful action.

The experience blends mobile and Apple Watch tracking to capture the way people actually move — walking to work, taking the stairs, biking, gardening, and more. Research made one thing clear: most people don’t connect with traditional gyms. They feel uncomfortable, unsure of the equipment, or simply too busy. Vigor meets them where movement already happens.
